methods.label: Combine tabulated powers
methods.explanation:
If ordinary arithmetic combinations of the tabulated values are permitted, we can improve on direct comparisons. Let \(x=\log_{10}2\). Because the base-ten logarithm is increasing and \(\log_{10}(2^k)=kx\), the table gives
\[
2^{10}=1024>1000=10^3
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad x>\frac3{10}.
\]
To obtain a smaller upper bound, cube another tabulated value:
\[
2^{33}=(2^{11})^3=2048^3
=8{,}589{,}934{,}592<10^{10}.
\]
Taking logarithms gives \(33x<10\). Hence
\[
\frac3{10}<x<\frac{10}{33}=\frac{40}{132}.
\]
This is the strongest listed interval: its upper endpoint satisfies
\[
\frac{10}{33}<\frac4{13}<\frac4{12}<\frac4{11},
\]
and its lower endpoint is greater than \(3/11\). Thus each other listed interval contains the interval in D.

If “only the tabular information” instead means that one may compare only unaltered table entries, the tightest direct comparisons are \(10^3<2^{10}\) and \(2^{13}<10^4\), giving choice C. That restriction is not stated. With ordinary arithmetic allowed, the strongest listed conclusion is \(\frac3{10}<\log_{10}2<\frac{40}{132}\), choice D.
